cross_package_notes.note: Verified read-only caller compatibility across internal/application/... and internal/handler/... via go vet -p 1: all exported symbols in access, attachment, chat_pipeline, credential, file, memory, retriever, and sandboxalloc preserve exact signatures.

invariants_checked: Workspace RBAC, KB owner-workspace checks, organization/share grant resolution, and API-key KB resource scopes fail closed on missing/zero TenantID, invalid required roles, or mismatched caller contexts.

ResolveKB, KBAccess.WithGrant, and KBAccess.Context verify caller identity against both materialized CallerContextKey and unmaterialized TenantIDContextKey / UserID / Principal / Role context values before minting grants or switching execution tenant.

ResolveKBFile, ResolveSessionFile, and ResolveAttachment enforce non-zero caller TenantID, grant-to-KB tenant consistency (KnowledgeBase.TenantID == EffectiveTenantID), stored resource catalog TenantID matching, and binding verification before returning physical storage paths.
AuthorizeKBAccess and KB search target resolution reject nil/zero-tenant KnowledgeBase records without panicking; zero legacy brand residues present.

findings.summary: ResolveKB, KBAccess.WithGrant, and KBAccess.Context only checked CallerContextKey when already materialized, allowing callers on contexts carrying only TenantIDContextKey/UserContextKey/Principal to mint grants or switch execution tenants across mismatched callers; ResolveKB also accepted zero kb.TenantID or invalid requiredRole values instead of failing closed.

callerMatchesContext allowed zero-value unauthenticated KBAccess.Caller (TenantID=0) to match an unauthenticated context in ResolveKBFile, ResolveKBFile did not verify grant.KnowledgeBase.TenantID == grant.EffectiveTenantID before resolving files, and AuthorizeKBAccess dereferenced nil *types.KnowledgeBase elements in target slices.

invariants_checked: Processor enforces strict tenant/session scoping, file size and MIME/extension validation, and bounded stream reads when ingesting, extracting text/OCR, and storing chat attachments.
Storage backend resolution and cleanup preserve physical-path isolation without leaking host paths or cross-tenant references; zero weknora/knora/wk_ residues present.
Concurrent attachment processing passes go test -race cleanly.

Plugin chain ordering across QueryUnderstand, ExtractEntity, Search, SearchEntity, Rerank, WikiBoost, WebFetch, Merge (including history merge and citation source expansion), DataAnalysis, FilterTopK, IntoChatMessage, and ChatCompletion/ChatCompletionStream preserves context boundaries and untrusted source-data framing.

getSearchResultFromHistory clones historical KnowledgeReferences so stored ChatManage.History entries are never mutated in place, and filterHistoryResults enforces current-turn SearchTargets / KnowledgeBaseIDs / KnowledgeIDs / WebSearchEnabled scope so revoked KBs, tag-restricted KBs without document proof, and disabled web-search results cannot leak from prior turns.

attachCitationSources requires non-empty ParentChunkID before recording or matching sibling parent links so unrelated top-level chunks (ParentChunkID == '') in the same document are never cross-linked.

Goroutines spawned by RunParallel, PluginSearch, PluginChatCompletionStream, and PluginWebFetch isolate panics via recover(), preventing single-plugin/provider panics from crashing the server process or deadlocking WaitGroups.

PluginWikiBoost guards nil kbService/entries and restricts score boosting strictly to chunks belonging to wiki-enabled target KBs; LLM/repository nil responses in chat_completion, query_understand, data_analysis, and extract_entity fail safely without nil-pointer dereferences.

findings.summary: filterHistoryResults and getSearchResultFromHistory re-injected prior-turn KnowledgeReferences without checking whether their KB, tag scope, or web_search source remained authorized in the current turn's SearchTargets/WebSearchEnabled, and mutated ChatManage.History[i].KnowledgeReferences in place.

attachCitationSources inserted empty c.ParentChunkID ('') into allowedParents and matched allowedParents[c.ParentChunkID] without requiring non-empty ParentChunkID, cross-linking unrelated top-level chunks from the shared byID map into another result's CitationSources.

Concurrent goroutines in RunParallel, PluginChatCompletionStream, PluginWebFetch, and PluginSearch lacked panic recovery (and nil client/page guards in WebFetch), allowing a panicking task, stream consumer, or web fetcher to crash the entire Go process or hang wg.Wait().

PluginWikiBoost boosted every ChunkTypeWikiPage result across all KBs whenever at least one target KB had wiki enabled (and panicked if kbService was nil), and chat_completion, query_understand, data_analysis, and extract_entity lacked nil-response guards on (nil, nil) adapter returns.

invariants_checked: OwnerFromContext resolves personal vault ownership strictly from CallerFromContext(ctx).TenantID (never a shared agent's execution tenant), rejects API-key scoped contexts, and allows only verified web_user and api_external_user principals.

Vault AES-GCM secret sealing binds TenantID, UserID, and ItemID into authenticated envelope metadata and verifies owner match on open so cross-tenant row tampering fails closed with ErrCredentialUnavailable and zero secret leakage in errors/logs.

HandleStore encrypts one-time and vault-backed secret handles in Redis under SYSTEM_AES_KEY, enforces non-zero Owner on Create/Resolve/Complete, and uses atomic Lua ownership verification before deleting handles in Complete.
Submitter validates non-zero Owner/prompt TenantID, validates stored SecureFormRequest schema before minting handles or vault items, and discards orphan handles on HITL resolution races.

findings.summary: HandleStore.Complete deleted Redis secret handles by sessionID + handle token without verifying tenantID or userID (allowing cross-user/cross-tenant handle destruction if session/handle IDs were observed) and HandleStore.Create accepted zero-value Owner.

OwnerFromContext read TenantIDFromContext(ctx) instead of CallerFromContext(ctx).TenantID (routing personal vault operations into a shared agent's execution tenant under WithExecutionTenant) and did not reject TenantAPIKeyScope contexts; Vault envelope sealing did not bind TenantID/UserID/ItemID against DB row tampering; Submitter.Submit lacked zero-owner and stored SecureFormRequest.Validate() guards.

invariants_checked: LocalFileService resolves ancestor and leaf components via Lstat + EvalSymlinks containment checks (resolveLocalPathNoSymlinks) across GetFile, DeleteFile, CopyFile, SaveFile, and SaveBytes, preventing symlink reads, writes, copies, or deletions outside baseDir.

All object storage backends (Local, MinIO, S3, COS, TOS, OSS, OBS, KS3) enforce non-zero tenantID, single-segment non-traversal knowledgeID, non-nil multipart FileHeader, SafeObjectKey validation, and SSRF-safe dialer/redirect policies.

COS bucket and region identifiers enforce strict RFC-1123 label validation (isValidCOSLabel) across primary and temp buckets so crafted bucket/region strings cannot break out of <bucket>.cos.<region>.myqcloud.com.

NewFileServiceFromStorageConfig fails closed when a non-empty Local.PathPrefix is invalid/traversal instead of silently falling back to root baseDir, and ResolveTenantFileServiceWithFallback safely handles nil tenant pointers.

findings.summary: LocalFileService.checkFilePath only performed lexical filepath.Abs/Rel prefix checks without os.Lstat or filepath.EvalSymlinks verification, allowing symlinks inside a tenant's local directory to read, overwrite, copy, or delete arbitrary host files outside baseDir.

newCosClient interpolated bucketName/region directly into fmt.Sprintf('https://%s.cos.%s.myqcloud.com') without RFC-1123 label validation (allowing URL authority breakout via '/', '@', '#', or dots), and SaveFile/SaveBytes/CopyFile across storage providers lacked zero-tenantID, traversal-knowledgeID ('../other-tenant'), and nil-*multipart.FileHeader guards.

NewFileServiceFromStorageConfig silently ignored invalid/traversal Local.PathPrefix values by falling back to root localBaseDir instead of failing closed, and ResolveTenantFileServiceWithFallback dereferenced nil *types.Tenant pointers in log fields on the fallback branch.

invariants_checked: Strict (tenant_id, user_id) scoping via callerScope/enabledScope isolates all personal conversational and long-term memories across Recall, Remember, Update, Forget, Search, List, Episodes, DocAffinity, Extraction, and Consolidation so User A's memories never leak into User B's prompts.
FamiliarKnowledgeIDs enforces workspace, agent, and user memory opt-out switches via enabledScope before returning document affinity boosts.

Recall falls back to persisted subject.BlockText only when loading active resident memories fails (residentErr != nil), never resurrecting archived/deleted memories when the resident query succeeds with zero active rows.

Under cross-workspace shared-agent execution (WithExecutionTenant), scopeModelContext re-binds ModelService calls to the caller's own workspace and ScheduleExtraction strips foreign chatModelID values so caller memory tasks never reference or invoke foreign workspace models.

findings.summary: Under shared-agent execution (WithExecutionTenant), memory embedding, topic resolution, consolidation, and extraction passed the foreign execution tenant's ctx (TenantIDContextKey / TenantInfoContextKey) to ModelService and persisted the foreign agent's chatModelID into the caller's async MemoryExtractPayload.

FamiliarKnowledgeIDs bypassed workspace, agent, and user memory opt-out switches by calling callerScope instead of enabledScope, and Recall fell back to stale subject.BlockText whenever resident == '' even when loadResidentText succeeded with zero active items after archival/deletion.

invariants_checked: VerifyBinding, CreateRetrieveEngineForKB, CreateRetrieveEngineFromPayload, resolveBoundEngine, and vectorStoreRepoOwnership.StoreOwnedBy enforce non-zero tenantID, non-blank storeID, and non-nil registry/ownership/tenantInfo dependencies fail-closed.

Store sentinels omit raw store UUIDs, backend endpoints, and credentials while preserving retryable (ErrVectorStoreUnavailable / context error) vs permanent (ErrVectorStoreForbidden / ErrVectorStoreNotFound) classification for async workers.

CompositeRetrieveEngine guards nil receivers, nil engineInfo/retrieveEngine entries, and nil *types.IndexInfo elements across Retrieve, SupportRetriever, BatchIndex, BatchIndexVectors, BatchUpdateChunkContent, ValidateKnowledgeIndexMove, and concurrentExecWithError under -race.

findings.summary: VerifyBinding and resolveBoundEngine did not reject tenantID == 0 or whitespace-only storeID strings fail-closed (allowing whitespace *vectorStoreID to bypass empty-string unbound normalization into GetOrLoadByStoreID), panicked on nil registry/ownership, and CreateRetrieveEngineForKB panicked on typed-nil *types.Tenant in context.

CompositeRetrieveEngine dereferenced nil engineInfo / retrieveEngine entries in concurrentExecWithError, Retrieve, BatchUpdateChunkContent, and ValidateKnowledgeIndexMove, and dereferenced nil *types.IndexInfo elements in BatchIndex and BatchIndexVectors.

invariants_checked: Service.Place validates non-zero SessionTenantID and non-blank SessionID and verifies session ownership via s.sessions.GetByID(ctx, req.SessionTenantID, req.SessionID) BEFORE returning an existing placement from Lookup, preventing cross-tenant session ID probing or shared UserMachine disclosure.
VerifySessionAllocation enforces active (unreleased) assignment, matching config/digest address, current session owner digest match, and current auth-source eligibility for shared user machines.

UserMachineGC coordinates single-replica scans via redislock, synchronizes renewer goroutine shutdown before lock release, skips Release when lock renewal fails, and fences Redis cursor writes/deletes with an atomic Lua lock-token check so a replica whose lock expired can never overwrite or delete a new holder's cursor.

findings.summary: Service.place returned existing assignments from unscoped Lookup(ctx, req.SessionID) before verifying s.sessions.GetByID(ctx, req.SessionTenantID, req.SessionID), allowing a cross-tenant caller supplying another tenant's placed SessionID to read back that tenant's Assignment and shared UserMachine identity.

UserMachineGC.saveCursor wrote/deleted UserMachineGCCursorKey via context.WithoutCancel(ctx) without fencing against the active UserMachineGCLockKey token (allowing a replica whose lock lease expired mid-scan to overwrite or DEL the new lock holder's cursor), and RunOnce did not synchronize renewer goroutine exit before releasing the lock.
